item.title: Mukta bodha intro
item.description: In the eleventh century, within works such as the Ciñciṇīmatasārasamuccaya, the various transmissions of the Classical Śākta tantras—especially the Trika, the Krama, and the Kubjikā traditions—begin to develop a new way of thinking about their relationship with each other. They emerge not as rivals, but as complementary. Nonetheless, they remain distinct parts of a dynamic and unified Classical Śākta tradition, organized in terms of three or more streams corresponding to the cardinal directions.
